promo: Welcome to Crewdesk: time tracking, projects and team chat, built for survey companies.
To show you around, we'll use Northgate Geomatics, a pretend company with fourteen surveyors and fourteen live projects.
Logging time is the heart of it. Pick the project you're on, press the big plus, and your time is being recorded.
The clock keeps running while you work, whether you started it on your phone in the field or on your computer in the office.
Every survey job lives in one place: topographic surveys, setting out, monitoring, measured building surveys and more.
Each project shows its planned hours against the hours actually logged, broken down by task and by person.
Manhole maps let you pin every chamber on a satellite map, with photos, levels and survey details attached.
When the job's done, export a manhole index, a labelled map, a full PDF report, or an Excel register for the client.
A shared calendar keeps site visits, possessions and deadlines where everyone can see them.
Chat with the crew in groups or direct messages, and send photos and files straight from site.
Managers can see who's working, what they're working on, and where, right now.
Timesheets build themselves from the time you log. Download one person's month, or the whole team's as a single zip.
Finished jobs move to the archive, filed by year, and each one can produce its own PDF report.
Hours and performance charts show how every job is tracking against its plan.
And anyone can send in ideas, report a problem, or ask HR a question.
That's Crewdesk. Less paperwork, more surveying.
home: This is Home, where you log your day as you go.
Start by picking the project you're working on. Your most recent projects are always near the top.
Then tap the big plus button to start the clock.
Choose the task and the type of work, such as fieldwork or office work, and add a short note if it helps.
If you forgot to press start, set the time you really began and the clock will count from then.
While the clock is running, the plus turns into a red square, so you can always see you're on the clock.
Moving on to a different job? Tap Change to pick another project, and the time is split for you.
Your recent projects sit at the top of the list, so switching only takes a tap.
Underneath, today's log builds itself. Tap any entry if you need to correct the times or details.
When you finish a piece of work, tap the square to stop the clock and say briefly what you did.
At the end of the day, press Finish for today.
Jot down what went well and what could be better. If you pressed it by mistake, there's an Undo, and your clock picks up where it left off.
That's your day logged, and it's already on your timesheet.
projects: Projects are the bigger jobs, and tasks are the pieces of work inside them.
Each project has its own colour and job number, so it's easy to spot across the app.
Open a project to see its tasks, the people working on it, and how it's progressing.
Here you can compare the planned hours with everything that's been logged so far.
Tap the play button on any task to start timing it straight away.
The tabs hold the project's timeline, photos, manhole maps and its own chat.
Add attachment lets you upload photos or create a new manhole map for this project.
The three-dot menu has the rest: archive the project, download its PDF report or timesheet, and more.
Finished jobs move to Archived, where they're sorted into folders by year.
Admins create new projects with the New project button.
Give it a name, a job number, the client, the site address and a colour, and it's ready for the team.
Plan the job, then log your time against it.
timesheet: Your timesheet is built for you, straight from the time you log.
It fills itself in, and updates live whenever you add or change time, even for days that have already passed.
The current month shows In progress. Earlier months show Completed, or Not complete if days are missing.
Tap any day to see its entries, your notes, and any overtime.
Missed something? Tap Add time, or tap an existing entry to change it.
Once a month is finished, tap Review timesheet to see exactly what the spreadsheet will look like.
Download the month as an Excel file named with your initials, or upload your own timesheet if your company uses a different one.
No more filling in timesheets on a Friday afternoon.
calendar: The calendar shows everything that's planned, at a glance.
The month view shows what's happening on each day.
Tap a day to see its events and tasks listed underneath.
Events, tasks and project dates all appear on the days they fall.
Switch to Week or List when you need more detail.
If you only want to see your own work, use Just me and the filters.
Admins can create named calendars, for example one for Gateshead and one for Warrington.
Everyone can then choose which calendars to show or hide.
Tap the plus button to add an event, and pick which calendar it belongs to.
Plan the week together with your team.
chat: Chat keeps you talking to your team, even when you're out on site.
Company chat, group chats and direct messages all live here.
Tap the paperclip to send a photo from your camera, a picture from your library, or a file like a PDF or drawing.
To copy or delete a message, press and hold it on your phone, or right-click it on a computer.
Admins can clear a whole chat when needed: tap the chat's name, then Clear chat history.
team: The Team page shows who's who in your company, and where things are happening.
The map shows every live project site. Tap a pin to open the site card.
Directions from here opens your phone's maps app with the route already set.
Tap the expand button to make the map full screen, and the cross to come back.
People is a dropdown. Tap it to see everyone in the company.
Teams sit underneath. Tap one to see who's in it, and join or leave it yourself.
Admins can rename a team by tapping its name, and add or remove members.
Your whole company, in one place.
suggest: Suggestions is where you send ideas, report problems, or ask HR a question.
Got an idea, spotted a bug, or need to ask HR something? Send it from here.
Pick the kind of message, write it out, and press send.
Admins reply, and you'll see their answer right here.
Admins see every message in Admin, under Suggestions.
admin: The admin dashboard is for owners and admins.
At the top you can see who's working right now, and what they're working on.
People shows everyone's hours and overtime for this month.
Under Timesheets, Current shows this month's timesheets, with any that aren't complete highlighted in red.
Completed months are filed automatically into the archive, by year and month.
If a timesheet is unfinished, the person and the admins get a reminder every Monday.
Your whole company, at a glance.
files: Files is where your company keeps its training documents, guides and forms.
Everything the team needs to know lives here, open to everyone in the company.
You can filter by category, like Training or Health and safety.
Or search by title, description, or file name to find what you need.
To add your own, give it a title, a category and a short description, then attach a photo and any files, such as PDFs or Word documents.
The first photo you add becomes the cover picture.
Anyone can open a resource, read it, and open or save its files to their device.
Manhole maps have their own folder, called Maps, at the top of Files.
Share what the team needs to know.
mhplot: This tutorial shows you how to plot manholes, whether you're on site or back in the office.
Open the map, and switch to Edit mode so you can add and move manholes.
Choose the manhole type first. It sets the colour and the icon of the pin.
Then tap Add manhole, and tap the map exactly where the cover is.
It's given the next reference number automatically, so you never need to keep count.
While you're there, add the cover level, invert level, depth and any other details.
Use Add photo to take pictures with your camera. They're attached to that manhole.
Standing right next to it on site? Choose Add manhole, then Use my GPS position, and it's placed where you're standing.
To move a manhole, just drag its pin. Everyone working on the map sees the change live.
If you already know the coordinates, open Coordinates, type them in, and press Add manhole here.
Tap, use GPS, or type coordinates, then fill in the details.
manholes: Manhole maps let you record every chamber on a satellite map.
You'll find every manhole map in Files, under Maps, or by opening a project and choosing its Maps tab.
Each pin is a manhole, coloured by its type and labelled with its reference.
Tap any pin to open its record.
Status, location, photos, notes and survey details are all kept together in one place.
To change anything, switch to Edit mode.
Update the status as the work progresses,
and fill in the levels, depth, material and condition.
To add a new one, pick its type, tap Add manhole, then tap the map.
On site, Use my GPS position drops it exactly where you're standing.
Drag any pin to move it. Everyone sees changes as they happen.
Use the search bar for an address, a postcode or a place. Results appear as you type, and Enter takes you straight there.
Tap 3D for a three-dimensional view. Drag to look around. On a computer, the side buttons move you closer, turn and tilt.
From the three-dot menu, Export gives you a labelled satellite map with a scale bar, a full report, or an Excel register.
Manhole types are shared across the whole company, and anyone can add their own.
From site to report, all in one place.
sheets: Spreadsheets and stats show money, hours and performance. They're for admins only.
Money shows your income and expenses, with a projection for the months ahead.
Hours breaks time down by month and type of work, by project, and by day of the week.
You can also see everyone's hours, overtime, and how their time splits between field and office.
Performance compares projects against their plan, counts tasks completed, and shows a typical working day.
Choose a date range at the top, from this month up to the last twelve months.
Know exactly how the work is going.
settings: This tutorial covers settings, search, and a few extras.
The More menu holds your timesheet, Files, these tutorials, and a demo company you can practise in.
In your profile, set your photo, name, job title and phone number.
Choose a light or dark look, and which tabs appear in your bar.
Admins have company settings too: invites, the working day, and permissions.
Search finds jobs, people, and even parts of the app. Try typing tutorials.
Set it up once, and it's ready to go.
lone: Stay safe keeps an eye on anyone working on their own.
Buddies and admins can see everyone who's working alone right now.
If someone misses a check-in, you get an urgent alert. Call them, open their location, or tap I'm responding.
Working alone yourself? Say where you are, how often to check in, and pick a buddy.
The dial counts down to your next check-in, and your phone buzzes when it's due.
Tap I'm safe to check in. You can add more time, or finish when you're done.
In trouble? Hold the red button for two seconds. It alerts everyone and sounds a loud siren.
Help is told straight away. Cancel the alert once you're safe.
Location is only shared from the Crewdesk Android app.
